SwotAxisStatement.description: Represents a statement for a SWOT axis (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats).

certainty.description: A score representing the certainty of the statement, ranging from 1 (least certain) to 10 (most certain).
certainty.title: Certainty

importance.description: A score representing the importance of the statement, ranging from 1 (least important) to 10 (most important).
importance.title: Importance

negative_statement.description: A statement describing a negative aspect (Weakness or Threat).
examples: Our production costs are higher than the industry average.
negative_statement.title: Negative Statement

positive_statement.description: A statement describing a positive aspect (Strength or Opportunity).
examples: Our product has a unique feature that competitors lack.
positive_statement.title: Positive Statement

score.description: A score representing the impact of the statement, from -5 (very negative) to 5 (very positive). A forced choice: there is no neutral 0 (the book's bipolar scale), so every statement takes a side.
score.title: Score

SwotAxisStatement.title: SwotAxisStatement

SwotCluster.description: An enumeration of the different clusters in a SWOT analysis.
SwotCluster.title: SwotCluster

SwotClusterResult.description: Represents the result of a SWOT analysis for a specific cluster.

axis_statements.description: Statements for the SWOT axis within the specified cluster: between 2 and 5.

axis_statements.title: Axis Statements

cluster.description: The cluster of the SWOT analysis(e.g., Value Proposition, Cost & Revenue, Infrastructure, Customer Interface).

opportunities.description: Identified opportunities for the specified cluster, each scored 1-5: between 1 and 7.

examples.text: Develop strategic partnerships with complementary businesses.

opportunities.title: Opportunities

threats.description: One rating per threat question of this cluster's catalog (2, 5, 7 or 7 questions depending on the cluster), each scored 1-5. Exactly the cluster's catalog, each question once, in any order.
threats.title: Threats

SwotClusterResult.title: SwotClusterResult

SwotOpportunity.description:
Represents a single Opportunity, per the BMG document's Evaluating
Business Models format (pp. 220-223): each generative question is
paired with a 1-5 scale. The book gives no caption for this scale; the
working interpretation used here is "how strongly this applies to this
model" (1 = barely, 5 = very strongly).

score.description: How strongly this applies to this model: 1 (barely) to 5 (very strongly). Interpretation is a project decision; the book's pages give the scale with no caption.
score.title: Score

text.description: The opportunity statement (typically phrased as, or derived from, one of the book's generative questions).
examples: Could we generate recurring revenues by converting products into services?
text.title: Text

SwotOpportunity.title: SwotOpportunity

SwotThreat.description:
Represents the rating of ONE question of the fixed threat catalog
(`ThreatQuestion`). Every SWOT iteration rates the same 21 questions, so
the sum of the scores is comparable between iterations. Same 1-5 scale
and working interpretation as `SwotOpportunity`.

question.description: Which catalog threat this rates. Each cluster must rate exactly the questions of its own catalog, once each.

score.description: How strongly this threat applies to this model: 1 (barely) to 5 (very strongly). Interpretation is a project decision; the book's pages give the scale with no caption.
score.title: Score

text.description: How this threat applies to this business model, in one or two sentences.
examples: Customers can switch to a cheaper app that covers the same basic need.
text.title: Text

SwotThreat.title: SwotThreat

ThreatQuestion.description:
The fixed catalog of 21 threats rated in every SWOT iteration, so the
threat part of `weighted_weakness_threat_score` always sums over the
same questions (range 21..105) and is comparable between iterations.
The values are stable contract ids. The comments are paraphrases, one
per question, of the threat the id stands for.
ThreatQuestion.title: ThreatQuestion
